AI-native Software, Computing Sciences and Electrical Engineering, Master of Science (2 yrs), autumn 2027
Faculty of Information Technology and Communication Sciences

kuvaus.en:
Strong and versatile foundation for your future career

AI-Native Software (MSc) provides students with a solid understanding of computer science and software engineering in a paradigm where AI systems act as collaborators in software development and as integral components of software systems. It covers the analysis, design, implementation, and continuous evolution of complex software systems, with AI, generative models, and autonomous agents supporting and transforming software engineering activities and decision-making. You will develop the skills to use AI effectively throughout the software development lifecycle, integrate AI into real-world applications, and critically evaluate its capabilities and limitations. The specialisation also develops your engineering judgment to build software systems that are reliable, responsible, and sustainable. Moreover, you can choose courses based on your interests to complement and deepen your expertise to shape the future of software in an AI-powered world.

Gain valuable insight from industry collaboration

An exceptionally large number of IT companies in the Tampere region provide an inspiring environment and opportunities to apply your skills and address fascinating real-life challenges. The research conducted at the Tampere Software Engineering Research Center and the AI research lab (GPT-Lab) further strengthens the programme’s emphasis on state-of-the-art methods and technologies. The close collaboration with industry ensures that the contents of the programme are both on a high level academically and relevant to your future career prospects.

Career prospects

Graduates of this specialization will be equipped to work in versatile roles that combine software engineering expertise with advanced AI capabilities, for example:

  • AI-native software engineer
  • AI systems architect 
  • Technology consultant or innovator 
  • Academic and research career 

Your skills will be relevant across industries where intelligent systems are transforming products, services, and operations.

AI-native Software is one of the specialisations in the Master’s Programme in Computing Sciences and Electrical Engineering.

osaamistavoitteet.en:
Upon completion of the AI-Native Software specialisation, you will understand AI-native software engineering and be able to design, develop, and improve high-quality software systems where AI is an integral part of the solution. You will be able to 

  • Develop and evaluate demanding AI-native software systems 
  • Apply AI-enabled methods and tools throughout software development 
  • Assess architectures, technologies, and trade-offs in AI-native systems 
  • Consider ethical, legal, security, and sustainability aspects 
  • Follow advances in software engineering and AI, supporting expert work, research, and doctoral studies.

teksti.en:
Applicants with a background in computer science or software engineering choose the AI-native Software specialisation to deepen their knowledge and skills in developing high-quality software in which AI is an integral part. The programme combines both academic and industry perspectives and covers the full lifecycle of software development, with AI supporting both software engineering activities and the systems being developed.

The studies address real-world problems and explore subjects such as requirements management, software system architecture, implementation, and testing and quality assurance, software project management, and the use of generative AI and autonomous agents in software development.

We offer our students the opportunity for a broad, cross-disciplinary education. A rich variety of minor subject studies is available. In fact, each degree is a unique combination of studies that the individual student has found most interesting.

Master’s Programme comprises of 120 ECTS credits. Each ECTS credit is about 27 hours of student work. Courses are worth 90 ECTS, and the remaining 30 ECTS are awarded for successfully completing a master’s thesis. The duration of the programme is two years. Students usually spend three semesters completing courses and one semester preparing the Master’s thesis. The studies start in late August, and the academic year ends in late May.

Master’s Programme in Computing Sciences and Electrical Engineering consists of 14 specialisations, leading either to Master of Science, or Master of Science in Technology degree:

  • Accessible and Sustainable Digital Services (MSc)
  • AI-native Software (MSc)
  • Communication Systems and Networks (MSc Tech)
  • Data Science (MSc)
  • Electrical Energy Engineering (MSc Tech)
  • Embedded Systems (MSc Tech)
  • Gamification and Engaging Technologies (MSc)
  • Information Security (MSc Tech)
  • Human-Technology Interaction (MSc)
  • Signal Processing and Machine Learning (MSc Tech)
  • Speech and Language Technology for AI (MSc Tech)
  • Statistical Data Analytics (MSc)
  • System-on-Chip Design (MSc Tech)
  • Wireless Communications and RF Systems (MSc Tech)

Detailed information on the content and structure of the studies is available in the curriculum.

A typical career in software engineering starts in a technical role, with opportunities to advance into expert and managerial positions. Software engineering offers a versatile career path to many domains from software service companies to large scale manufacturing. Our graduates find employment also in commercial and administrative tasks relating to the field, without excluding work as a researcher or a teacher. 

Following the successful completion of the programme, our graduates will be eligible to apply for admission to doctoral programmes in Finland or abroad.

In addition to studies in one’s own Master’s Programme, students may take full advantage of the teaching offered by the Tampere higher education community ranging from technical to vocational studies in various fields.
This master's degree provides the required background if you wish to pursue doctoral studies, available at Tampere University. There are no tuition fees in doctoral studies.

opetuskieletKuvaus.en: The official language of the programme is English, meaning that all the courses, exams and student services are arranged in English. Consequently, proficiency in both written and spoken English is an absolute prerequisite. Students are required to submit an approved certificate of their language proficiency when applying for admission. In addition, students are required to complete a course in the Finnish language. The course provides them with an introduction into everyday Finnish and Finnish culture.

kuvaus.en:
You will need to upload scanned copies of the original documents as attachments to the application form. In addition to the general application attachments, there may be additional programme-specific attachments that are needed when applying.

All the required attachments are mandatory, and missing attachments may lead to a rejection in student selection. Submit the attachments as instructed on the Application documents webpage.

You can edit your application only during the application period. Attachments can be uploaded until 14 January 2027 at 23.59 (UTC+2).

In addition to the Tampere University general application attachments, for the Master's Programme in AI-native Software, Computing Sciences and Electrical Engineering, you may submit an additional document listing one or more publicly accessible project repository links, such as GitHub repositories, for projects you have conducted or been involved. For each project, include a brief description of no more than 50 words, covering:

  • When was it conducted
  • What was it about
  • The applicant’s role in the project

This document is optional and intended for students who wish to showcase relevant project repositories.
